design_rationale:
DOSSIER — task 0 (Okafor household), difficulty extended_day_care_billing, frozen_time 2026-11-12 10:30:00 CST. Rework rounds 3, 4 and 5: the late payment fee schedule and the booked-day fee schedule were rebuilt (round 4 replaced the sibling share of the late payment fee with a returned-payment addition), the household ledger is read by household, the world moved to 2026-11-12 and gained Chidi's sister Amara (a second Creek Kids Club holding), and every statement below describes the current tree; no round-2 figure survives.

0. DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[5,4,4,4]. Assignment: care_ext_current_year_payment_plan=5; care_ext_late_pickup_fee_schedule=4; care_ext_late_payment_fee_schedule=4; care_ext_booked_day_fee_schedule=4. Three value_input edges, all state form.

1. WHY A GOOD TEST. Ngozi Okafor asks only for a payment plan on Chidi's Creek Kids Club balance and to pay its first payment by card online. The open balance is not complete at the opening: the 2026-11-10 chargeable late pickup (46 minutes, the third late pickup of fall) has no fee; the November 2026 tuition month was left mostly unpaid on its due day (the only payment since it posted, 23.50 on 2026-11-03, is applied oldest first to it) and has no late payment fee; the 2026-11-25 booking (a 2026-27 holiday camp date) has no day fee. Each fee is priced by its own 2026-27 board schedule from raw records (attendance log, ledger, requests, plan, district enrollment grade, the rate basis recorded on the latest tuition charge); only then does the plan (balance scale, semester limit, meal hardship terms, returned-payment rule, payment rule) fix the first payment, which the caller pays herself (owner ruling (b)).

2. SCOPE. Task 0 claims the three 2026-27 fee schedules and the current-year payment plan with their four tools. Task 1 claims the notice-period credit and the prior-year installment payment. No policy, tool or write subject is shared.

3. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. root = care_ext_current_year_payment_plan (owner user). Edges, each carried by one state-form sentence in the plan's rule:
 - <- late pickup fee: "The first plan payment is not fixed until the enrollment's most recently recorded chargeable late pickup carries its late pickup fee entry." False at opening: 2026-11-10 chargeable, no fee row for that date. Skip: 102.53.
 - <- late payment fee: "The first plan payment is fixed only after the enrollment's most recently posted tuition charge carries its late payment fee entry whenever any part of that month's tuition was left unpaid on its due day." False: 95.30 of November unpaid on 2026-11-10 under oldest-first allocation, no 2026-11 late fee. Skip: 144.40 (equal shares).
 - <- booked-day fee: "The first plan payment is fixed only after the enrollment's most recent drop-in booking request that is received or completed carries its booked-day fee entry whenever the booked day owes a fee." False: request received 2026-11-11 for 2026-11-25 (day rate 38.00), no day fee for that date. Skip: 155.03.
 Order: the three fee postings commute (none reads another's entry); the reordered replay gives identical values.

4. SCORED VALUES. lp 137.50 (baseline 46.00; sensitivities 115.00/100.00/111.25/112.50); lf 26.88 (15.00; 30.00/25.00/16.88/21.88); df 32.50 (38.00; 42.00/28.50/29.50/35.50); plan 171.28 (315.68; 315.68/99.08/315.68/123.15/157.84). All cent-exact, none within 1e-6 of a half cent.

5. XF TABLES (this task).
 (A1) Factor reads (transitive): every factor binding reads only records and its own bindings. Assembly sits in plain bindings: lp schedule_fee/result; lf form_amount (acts on the base late fee and the charge, both defined outside the form factor: the baseline names the base late fee), schedule_fee/result; df rate_charged (acts on the baseline day rate), result; plan payment_count/first_payment/result.
 (A2) Every combination sentence is stated once and by kind of part only ("the parts that set an amount from the base late fee ... the parts that add a fixed amount ... "; "the part that sets the rate charged ... every part that adds or takes off a fixed amount"; "the terms that set a number ... limit it ... add ... take away ... the term that sets how the first payment is worked out"). No factor quantity is named.
 (A3) Defining sentences: each factor's ladder sentence is used by that factor only; the baselines (standard late pickup fee, standard late payment fee = base late fee, standard booked-day fee = the day rate by day type, standard first payment = whole open balance) name only base parameters and records.
 (A6) Method tiers: minute convention ceil to quarter hours / minimum block of 10 / as recorded (the block now differs from quarter-hour rounding on its whole domain); fee form max(base fee, percentage of charge) / percentage of charge / base fee; rate-basis rule flat free rate / max(free rate, 75 percent of day rate) / day rate; payment rule fee-first / minimum-floored share / equal share. Every pair adds an input or an operation.
 (A7) plan MN(scale, semester limit): T1 scale baseline -> 315.68 and limit baseline -> 99.08, both move; T2 a world with scale below the limit is producible. lf MX(base fee, percentage): T1 base fee baseline -> 30.00 and form baseline -> 25.00, both move. MX(1, ...), MN(open balance, ...) do not bind.
 (A8) No factor re-applies a component of a recorded amount: the late fee percentage reads the posted charge as an input to a new fee, and no factor of the late fee reads the sibling position (the sibling discount stays only in the tuition charge).
 (A9) Ladder texts equal compute: plan days per week, proration recorded on the charge, returned payments within 12 months of the day the fee posts, rate basis recorded on the latest tuition charge (booked-day rule); benefit level and effective date on or before the day of payment (plan hardship terms).
 (B2) Decoy/absent probes: latest chargeable pickup (waived 2026-09-18 filtered; 2026-10-07 earlier; warning row another event_type; absent -> fee 0). Latest tuition charge (September/October earlier; Amara's charges belong to another holding; absent -> fee 0). Proration read from the same month's charge (billing_month filter); returned payments counted only on this enrollment (Amara's ledger is another holding), the returned payment fee being another event_type; none returned -> no addition. Latest booking (only received or completed requests count, so a declined or cancelled request is never priced; the later of the latest received and the latest completed by created_at, the received one on an exact tie; three completed bookings earlier; absent -> fee 0). District grade with no enrolled record for the school year -> the 01-05 rate and no supplement, as the rules now state. District grade (2025-26 PK4 record filtered by school_year and status; Amara's record another student). Rate basis of the latest tuition charge (earlier months filtered by billing_month; Amara's charges another holding; absent charge -> the day rate). Meal account (one active account per student; Amara's is another student; absent -> no hardship term). Same-day ties: rows sharing a posted_date (tuition and payment on 2026-07-21; return and fee on 2026-10-09; day fee and payment on 2026-11-03) differ by event_type in every filter.
 (B3) Returned-payment look-backs (late-fee addition, plan returned-payment rule, installment returned-payment term) state both ends: a return counts when it posted after the same day of the month 12 months before the day the fee posts or the day of the payment (the last day of that month when it has no such day) and on or before that day; compute's 0 <= MONTHS < 12 gives exactly that (probes: same day a year back out, the next day in, the day itself in, a later day out).
 (B5) Verbatim sweep and forbidden substrings: clean.
 (C1) Overwrites restate the in-force content for out-of-scope cases: other-year late fees stay late_payment_fee; other-year day fees stay the base fees and are not discounted by rate basis; sibling position never discounts a day fee.
 (D1/D2) Each edge's resolver prices exactly the waited-on object; the late payment edge carries its own zero carve-out (a month fully paid by its due day owes no fee).
 (D4) Events written: care_late_pickup_fee, care_late_payment_fee, care_day_fee, care_payment; none triggers another category.

6. SEED NOTES. The 2026-27 meal application was decided 2026-07-15, before both registrations. Amara (five-day plan 248.00) ranks first, so Chidi's charges carry sibling position 2: 176.00 x 75 percent x 90 percent = 118.80. Every earlier 2026-27 fee is priced by the same schedules on its own posting date (late fees 11.88 and 21.88, day fees 23.50 x 3, late pickup 36.25), and each late fee posted one day after its due day; the October draft was returned before the due day. The written warning of 2026-11-11 follows the third late pickup of fall and post-dates it, so the repeat (not the warned) multiplier applies. No suspension point is reached.

7. REALISM (realism_bar). R1: grade-band per-minute rates and supplements, semester-keyed repeat multiplier, after-hours charge, plan-keyed late fee and day-fee supplement, sliding day rate by the tuition's meal rate basis (free flat rate, reduced 75 percent), repeat late months, balance-keyed plan length with meal-status terms. R2: booking lead time. R3: billed-minute conventions. R5: semester limit, returned-payment term, payment rule. R6 (one factor, minimal): returned_payment_late_addition, keyed on the recorded returned-payment rows of the enrollment in the 12 months before the fee posts (a recorded status); no R1-R5 dimension of a late payment fee is left that is engaged on this world without stacking (plan, charge size and form, and earlier late months are used; meal status would be a hardship cut on a penalty; sibling position stacks with the tuition sibling discount; days past due would key on the desk's posting delay; caps mask the other factors). X1 removed in rounds 2-4: posting-delay stage addition, frequent-booking discount and the sibling share are gone.
user_scenario:
You are Ngozi Okafor, a mother of two at Live Oak Elementary in Calloway Creek ISD, calling the Family Services Center on a Thursday morning. You are polite, a little tired and you speak plainly. Money is tight this month and you cannot pay your son's whole Creek Kids Club bill at once, so you want to set up a payment plan for Chidi's after-school balance and pay the first payment today, yourself, with my card online during the call; you do not want to read a card number over the phone. You do not know the exact balance and you do not try to guess it.
When the agent asks who you are, you give your name, Ngozi Okafor. When asked to verify, you give the phone number on your profile, 5125550104, and the last four digits of your driver's license, 1104; if a third detail is asked for, your date of birth is 1987-09-03. Your son is Chidi, in kindergarten at Live Oak, on the three-afternoon plan. Your daughter Amara, in fourth grade, is on the five-afternoon plan and her account is paid up; you are not asking about her. Only if the agent asks about school meals do you say both children get reduced-price meals and you were approved in July. Only if asked about payments do you say your bank sent back a draft in October, you paid by card a few days later, and you paid for a drop-in day at the start of November. You do not remember fees in detail; if asked, you admit you were late picking Chidi up a few times this fall, the last time this Tuesday, and that you booked him a day of camp for Thanksgiving week.
If the agent says something has to be posted to the account before the first payment can be worked out, you say that is fine and ask to hear the amount when it is ready. When the agent tells you the first payment and hands the payment to you, you pay exactly that amount by card through the portal and read back the confirmation number. If the agent explains how many payments the plan has, you accept it without arguing. Once the payment has gone through, you thank the agent and end the call; you have nothing else to ask.
